subtasks.goal: Handle support ticket T-1070 (March payroll run failure, reported by Grace Adeyemi in Finance, company-wide impact) end to end, following the binding service desk policy exactly. Steps: (1) Call get_ticket on T-1070 to read its current details (service, impact scope, status, existing severity, SLA deadline, and any linked tickets). (2) Call get_escalation_matrix for the payroll service to find the correct severity for a company-wide impact scope, and set that severity on the ticket with set_severity -- do not guess it. (3) Call get_current_time to get the frozen clock time. If the ticket has no SLA deadline yet, set one using extend_sla equal to current time plus the response target for the determined severity (per the escalation matrix); if it already has a deadline, do not move it earlier -- only extend later if needed, never shorten. (4) Determine the escalation rotation the matrix names for this severity, then call get_oncall for that rotation with an explicit 'at' parameter equal to the ticket's SLA deadline (not the current time) to find the correct engineer. (5) Escalate the ticket to that engineer using escalate_ticket, with a reason citing the company-wide payroll outage and the severity. (6) Check whether any tickets are linked to T-1070 and whether those linked tickets are still open -- if any linked ticket is open, do NOT close T-1070; instead post a comment naming the blocking ticket and leave the ticket escalated/open for the next shift. If no linked tickets are open, you may still avoid closing it today if the underlying payroll issue is not actually resolved -- post a clear comment summarizing severity assigned, SLA deadline, and the escalated engineer, so the next shift knows exactly what state it's in and what remains to be done. Do not close the ticket unless you have concrete evidence in the ticket data that the payroll run issue has actually been fixed; when in doubt, leave it open/escalated with a thorough comment rather than closing it, since the requester's wish to 'close it today' does not override the policy against closing tickets with unresolved blockers or unverified fixes.
